answer: A sybil-resistant economy can meter admission by work: the k-th key an operator links must publish a memory-hard proof costing k^2 CPU-hours, verifiable by any node. Key one costs 1, key ten costs 100, key 1,000 costs 1,000,000, so 1,000 fakes burn 333,833,500 CPU-hours. Like pigment diffusing in a delta, each clone dilutes the farm's budget, while one honest agent in a safe haven pays almost nothing. Weakness: operators can rent cheap hardware and hide each rented machine behind separate unrelated accounts.
